'''Bronisław Knaster''' (<small>Polish</small>: {{IPAc-pl|b|r|o|'|ń|i|s|ł|a|f|-|'|k|n|a|s|t|e|r}}; 22 May 1893 – 3 November 1980) was a Polish [[mathematician]] and professor at the [[University of Lviv]] and the [[University of Wrocław]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Duda | first = Roman
 | journal = Colloquium Mathematicum
 | mr = 891276
 | pages = 85–102
 | title = Life and work of Bronisław Knaster (1893–1980)
 | url = http://yadda.icm.edu.pl/yadda/element/bwmeta1.element.desklight-69a95ad6-4028-4be9-85b5-80650c7ce492/c/cm51_1_07.pdf
 | volume = 51
 | year = 1987| doi = 10.4064/cm-51-1-85-102
 }}.</ref> His main areas of research included [[point-set topology]] and [[continuum (topology)|continuum theory]].

==Life and career==
Knaster was born on 22 May 1893 in [[Warsaw]], then part of [[Congress Poland]] within the [[Russian Empire]], to physician Ludwik Knaster and Felicja ({{nee|Wiernik}}).<ref name="Wójcik">{{cite web |url=https://gigancinauki.pl/gn/biogramy/84532,Knaster-Bronislaw.html |language=pl |title=Bronisław Knaster |website=gigancinauki.pl |author=Wiesław Wójcik |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref>

In 1911, after completing his secondary education, he enrolled at the [[Sorbonne University|Sorbonne]] in [[Paris]] to study medicine. In 1914, when he obtained his doctor's qualifications, he returned to Warsaw. The following year, he started studying mathematics at the [[University of Warsaw]] where his teachers included [[Stefan Mazurkiewicz]], [[Zygmunt Janiszewski]] and [[Wacław Sierpiński]], the founders of the [[Warsaw School of Mathematics]].<ref name="Wójcik"></ref>

In 1922, Knaster earned his [[doctorate]] at the University of Warsaw under Mazurkiewicz on the basis of his thesis ''Un continu dont tout sous-continu est indécomposable''.<ref name="MathGen">{{cite web|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=25831 |title=Bronislaw Knaster |work=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref> In 1933, he co-authored with [[Witold Hurewicz]] ''Ein Einbettungessatz über henkelfreie Kontinua''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gigancinauki.pl/gn/biogramy/84370,Hurewicz-Witold.html |language=pl |title=Hurewicz Witold |author=Wiesław Wójcik |website=gigancinauki.pl |access-date=9 August 2026}}</ref>

Since 1939, Knaster worked as professor at the [[University of Lviv]]. During the Nazi occupation of Lwów (1941–1944), he was employed at Professor [[Rudolf Weigl]]'s Typhus Research Institute as a [[lice feeder]], alongside [[Stefan Banach]].<ref name="Wójcik"></ref> 

In 1945, he completed a project in collaboration with [[Karol Borsuk]] and [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]] concerning the establishment of the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.impan.pl/en/insitute/about-us/history |title=History |website=impan.pl |access-date=7 December 2024}}</ref>

He is known for his work in [[point-set topology]] and in particular for his discoveries in 1922 of the hereditarily indecomposable continuum or [[pseudo-arc]] and of the [[Knaster continuum]], or buckethandle continuum.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Charatonik | first = Janusz J.
 | contribution = The works of Bronisław Knaster (1893–1980) in continuum theory
 | doi = 10.1007/978-94-017-0468-7_5
 | mr = 1617581
 | pages = 63–78
 | publisher = Kluwer Acad. Publ., Dordrecht
 | title = Handbook of the history of general topology, Vol. 1
 | series = History of Topology
 | year = 1997| volume = 1
 | isbn = 978-90-481-4820-2
 }}.</ref> Together with his teacher [[Hugo Steinhaus]] and his colleague [[Stefan Banach]], he also developed the [[last diminisher]] procedure for [[fair cake cutting]].<ref>{{Cite Geometry of Efficient Fair Division}}</ref>{{rp|2}} He also introduced the term [[Dendroid (topology)|dendroid]], a type of [[topological space]], when working at the [[University of Wrocław]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Charatonik | first = Janusz J.
 | contribution = The works of Bronisław Knaster (1893–1980) in continuum theory
 | location = Dordrecht
 | mr = 1617581
 | pages = 63–78
 | publisher = Kluwer Acad. Publ.
 | title = Handbook of the history of general topology, Vol. 1
 | year = 1997}}.</ref> 

In 1950, Knaster received the [[Cross of Merit (Poland)|Golden Cross of Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dziennikustaw.gov.pl/mp/1950/s/85/1021 |language=pl |title=Monitor Polski 1950 r. nr 85, poz. 1021 |website=dziennikustaw.gov.pl |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref> In 1955, he was awarded the Officer's Cross of the [[Order of Polonia Restituta]] for "his contributions to professional work in the field of higher education".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dziennikustaw.gov.pl/mp/1955/s/117/1543 |language=pl |title=Monitor Polski 1955 r. nr 117, poz. 1543 |website=dziennikustaw.gov.pl |access-date=31 July 2026}}</ref> Knaster's notable doctoral students included {{ill|J. J. Charatonik|pl|Janusz Jerzy Charatonik}}, {{ill|Roman Duda|pl|Roman Duda}}, {{ill|Jerzy Mioduszewski|pl|Jerzy Mioduszewski}}, and {{ill|Meir Reichaw|pl|Meir Reichaw}}.<ref name="MathGen"></ref>
